# Capture/scripted setup grants loadout to the player only, so HUD upgrade rows omit it

> **Discovered while addressing AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9** (discovered-from:AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9) — the capture/scripted-setup counterpart of the hangar-war deployment fix.

## Problem statement

`applySceneSetup` (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`) grants capture/scripted setup
weapons only through `Player.equipWeapon(id, true)`, bypassing the
`EffectsRegistry`. Gyms that render the shared HUD build their upgrade rows from
`EffectsRegistry.activeWeapons()`, so a capture's permanent weapon has no row in
the upgrade list. The slot budget (`Loadout n/6`) counts it, but the visible list
does not — the same mismatch that AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9 fixed on the hangar-war
deployment path.

## Users

**Player running a gym with a capture setup that grants permanent weapons.**

> As a player running a gym whose capture setup grants permanent weapons, when I
> see the HUD upgrade list I expect it to show every permanent weapon I start
> with, so the list matches the `Loadout n/6` count and I can see what I have.

**Maintainer / future agent.**

> As a maintainer, I want capture/scripted setup permanent grants to run through
> the same grant seam as every other permanent grant, so the HUD, the player
> levels and the effect state can never drift apart again.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A gym (or scene) that applies a capture setup containing permanent weapons via
  `applySceneSetup` reports one slot-counted HUD upgrade row per granted weapon,
  matching a live-play run granted the same weapons through
  `grantPermanentWeapon`.
- The setup applier's documented ability to pre-grant more than
  `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` kinds is preserved (the capture divergence is unchanged).
- A regression test covers a setup-granted permanent weapon reaching both the
  `Player` and the `EffectsRegistry`.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Gyms that apply a capture setup with permanent weapons show those weapons in the
HUD upgrade list, so the list and the `Loadout n/6` count agree at a glance —
the same parity the hangar-war fix achieved for deployed loadouts.

## Constraints

- **The fix belongs in the shared applier `applySceneSetup`.** Gyms are the
  consumers; the applier lives in `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`. No gym is
  changed directly — only the applier's seam interface.
- **One permanent-grant seam.** Grants go through `grantPermanentWeapon`
  (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts`) — the shared seam already used by hold-full
  rewards and checkpoint-resume replay.
- **The six-slot cap divergence stays.** A setup may pre-grant more than
  `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` kinds; the applier never consults the slot pool (AH-0MVVJS34M00551ES).
- **No second HUD data path.** The fix must not make the HUD derive weapon rows
  from the slot model; the HUD keeps rendering registry state.
- **Gyms with no player remain unchanged.** `applySceneSetup` already returns
  early for `getPlayer() === null`; no additional guard needed.
- **`hangarDeployment.ts` stays Phaser-free.** The registry reaches the applier
  through a structural seam, matching the pattern established by that module.

## Existing state

- `applySceneSetup` (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`) loops
  `setup.player.weapons` calling `player.equipWeapon(id, true)` — no registry
  grant. Same pattern for `weaponLevels`.
- Gyms call it via `{ getPlayer: () => this.player }` or `{ getPlayer: () => null }`;
  no registry seam is passed today.
- `CombatCoreScene._adoptCaptureSetup` (:336) is the central gym caller — it
  passes `this.player` from a `CombatCoreScene` subclass.
- `PlayScene` (:1419) also calls `applySceneSetup` with `this.player`.
- `grantPermanentWeapon` (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts:80`) has the signature
  `(weaponId, effectsRegistry, player)` — exactly the two-surface grant needed.
- `PermanentWeaponRegistry` (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts:60`) exposes
  `applyWeapon(id, permanent?): boolean` — a minimal structural interface that
  `EffectsRegistry` satisfies.
- **Precedent fix for the identical class of bug on the hangar-war path:**
  AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9 extended `HangarWarDeploymentSeams` with an optional
  registry seam and routed through `grantPermanentWeapon`.
- The hangar-war fix (`applyHangarWarDeployment`) still only grants through the
  registry seam it now exposes — it does **not** call `player.equipWeapon` itself,
  delegating entirely to `grantPermanentWeapon`. The scripted setup currently
  grants **only** through `player.equipWeapon`, so both surfaces (registry +
  player) must be touched.

## Desired change

1. Extend `SceneSetupSeams` with an optional effects registry seam
   (e.g. `getEffectsRegistry(): PermanentWeaponRegistry | null`).
2. In `applySceneSetup`, replace each
   `player.equipWeapon(id as WeaponId, true)` call for `setup.player.weapons`
   with `grantPermanentWeapon(id, registry, player)` — same for `weaponLevels`
   (one call per level).
3. Gyms and `PlayScene` that call `applySceneSetup` pass the registry through the
   new seam; callers without a player (or without a registry) keep today's
   behaviour.
4. Update the module doc-comment to state that setup grants are permanent grants
   through the shared seam.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts` — add the registry seam to `SceneSetupSeams`;
  route `applySceneSetup` through `grantPermanentWeapon`; update the module
  comment.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — pass `this.effectsRegistry` (or the
  structural equivalent) into the updated `applySceneSetup` call in
  `_adoptCaptureSetup`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — pass `this.effectsRegistry` into the updated call.
- `src/powerups/choiceReward.ts` — the seam consumed (`grantPermanentWeapon`);
  expect no change beyond a possible doc cross-reference.
- `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.test.ts` — extend to assert both the player grant
  and the registry grant for a setup-applied weapon.
- `src/scenes/gym/gymSceneSetupAdoption.test.ts` — extend existing gym tests to
  assert the registry grant.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — setup / capture section: grants are permanent
  grants through the shared seam and render as HUD rows.

## Risks & assumptions

- **A1 — the registry is the right store, not the HUD.** Same assumption as
  AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9: registering the grant (not a HUD-side fallback) is
  correct, per the documented single-seam precedent.
- **A2 — no double counting.** `grantPermanentWeapon` calls both
  `registry.applyWeapon(id, true)` and `player.equipWeapon(id, true)` — exactly
  the two surfaces the current code touches individually. No extra state is
  created.
- **Risk — callers without a registry.** Gyms like `GymHangar`,
  `GymCurveSequencer`, and `GymHexWar` pass `getPlayer: () => null` (no player).
  The new seam is optional; when absent the applier keeps today's behaviour
  (a no-op for these callers, which is correct since they have no HUD).
- **Risk — callers with a player but no registry seam.** Any gym that creates a
  player but does not supply a registry will lose the HUD row again. All combat
  gyms that have players should supply the registry; non-combat gyms (no player)
  are unaffected.
- **Risk — `weaponLevels` grant count.** A weapon with `weaponLevels[id] = n`
  currently calls `equipWeapon` n times; `grantPermanentWeapon` must also be
  called n times to match. The level increment (run-scoped) must remain correct.
- **Scope-creep risk.** The hangar-war deployment (`applyHangarWarDeployment`)
  was fixed in AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9; no change to that module. Timed weapons
  (`timedWeapons`) are intentionally left as non-permanent (`equipWeapon(id,
  false)`) — they are not permanent grants and should not be routed through
  `grantPermanentWeapon`.

## Related work

- AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9 — "Hex War doesn't add initial loadout to slots" (the
  hangar-war deployment fix — same pattern, different surface; committed as
  part of v0.1.21).
- AH-0MVSHI07B003BZIP — "When continuing HUD upgrades list is empty" (the
  checkpoint-resume precedent — permanent grants must touch registry + player;
  commit `4d9daf0b`).
- AH-0MVVJS34M00551ES — "Six-slot cap and the setup applier divergence"
  (documents why the applier is allowed to exceed the cap).
- AH-0MVVJSE9800339S6 — "Document six-slot HUD presentation and setup
  divergence".
- AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX — "Loadout can exceed the six-slot cap" (the slot cap
  guard).

## Duplicate-work check

Searched `setup HUD weapon row`, `applySceneSetup permanent weapon`, `capture loadout HUD`,
`scripted setup HUD row`, `sceneSetup effects registry`. The closest completed items
are AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9 (hangar-war deployment — same class of bug, different surface)
and AH-0MVSHI07B003BZIP (checkpoint resume — same class of bug, same class of fix).
None satisfies this item's acceptance criteria: the `applySceneSetup` → registry →
HUD path is unfixed. This is **not** a duplicate.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Should `timedWeapons` also be routed through `grantPermanentWeapon`?**
  — Answer: no. Timed weapons are `equipWeapon(id, false)` (non-permanent,
  countdown-based). `grantPermanentWeapon` is specifically for permanent grants.
  Timed weapons should not appear in the permanent HUD upgrade list. Source:
  `sceneSetup.ts` line `equipWeapon(id as WeaponId, false)`; the distinction is
  intentional.
- **Q: Does `CombatCoreScene` already hold a reference to the effects registry?**
  — Answer: yes — `CombatCoreScene` extends `Phaser.Scene` and has
  `this.effectsRegistry` (an `EffectsRegistry` instance) as a member, inherited
  from the scene composition. The seam can pass it structurally. Source:
  `CombatCoreScene.ts` member declarations.
- **Q: Are there any callers that pass a player but intentionally omit the registry?**
  — Answer: all combat gyms that create a player also compose an effects registry
  (they extend `CombatCoreScene` or implement the same seam). Non-combat gyms
  (`GymHangar`, `GymCurveSequencer`, `GymHexWar`) pass `getPlayer: () => null`.
  No known caller creates a player without a registry. Source: gym source files.
- **Q (open): None blocking.** No producer decision required. The fix approach
  follows the documented shared-seam precedent exactly.

# Tests: one-level deployment semantics (AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A child 1)

**Test-first item.** Pin the *new* deployment semantics in tests **before** any
production change lands, so the harness change in the sibling item is driven by
a failing specification rather than by convention.

Parent: Re-measure ring timing for one-level hex deployments
(AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A). Blocked by **In HexMap killing the mini-boss wins the
hex (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2)**: the behaviour under measurement does not exist on
`dev` yet, so this item is parked rather than closed.

## Context

`createArenaDeploymentRunner` (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`) currently plays the
**classic campaign slice** (`campaign: true`, `campaignLevels:
campaignFromLevel(campaign, request.level)`) and derives a deployment's length
from `result.ticksSimulated × dt`, with `captured = result.won ||
result.ticksSimulated >= request.ticks` — i.e. "survived the 300 s window".
That model no longer describes the game: a deployment is one hex, one level,
played as a **five-wave sortie** (the level's first four regular waves plus its
mini-boss on wave 5).

The arena **already** supports the seam this needs: per-level mode
(`runArena({ level })`, `buildLevelWavePlan`) emits `level_cleared` on the tick
the final wave is detected clear (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`, per-level wave gate),
and the event record carries `tick`. Per-level mode keeps ticking after the
level clears and its `won` is `lives > 0 && aliveHostiles === 0` (a lingering
asteroid keeps it false), so **neither `ticksSimulated` nor `won` may be used**

## Context

The committed baseline (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`) models a
deployment as the campaign **slice** from the hex's aggression-selected level to
the campaign's final boss. The mini-boss ending (AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2) turns a
deployment into exactly one campaign level — a **five-wave sortie** (the
level's first four regular waves plus its mini-boss on wave 5,
`truncateCampaignForDeployment`), so every measured number and every derived ring window moves. This
item changes the model; it does **not** change the aggression mapping
(`hexDifficultyProfile`), the authored ring data, the loadout resolution, the
retake chance or the 2-minute between-sortie allowance.

## Desired change

1. `createArenaDeploymentRunner` (`src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts`) plays the
   **shipped one-level deployment**: `runArena` in per-level mode at
   `request.level` (the hex's aggression-selected level), keeping the launch
   `startingLoadout`, the seeded balance config and the existing tick cap as the
   run's safety bound.
2. The deployment's **duration** comes from the arena's `level_cleared` event
   tick (`× dt`) — never from `ticksSimulated` and never from `won`, both of
   which describe the tick loop rather than the level.
3. The **outcome** is `captured` when `level_cleared` was observed and `loss`
   when the player died before it.
4. The **retry allowance** charges the replayed deployment's own measured
   length (`measuredMinutes × retriesPerLoss`) instead of the flat
   `DEFAULT_RETRY_MINUTES` (300 s). `DEFAULT_RETRY_MINUTES` must no longer be
   the retry price; either delete it or redefine it as an explicitly documented
   fallback/sensitivity knob with no default use.
5. The **re-capture allowance** (rush line) charges a re-capture the line's
   measured mean deployment + the 2-minute visit, replacing the retired
   18 000-tick window (producer ruling Q1 = a on the parent item).
6. The module documentation and code comments state the new model end to end
   (`## What is measured, what is modelled` and `## Fidelity boundary`): one
   level played as the shipped **five-wave sortie** (the first four regular waves
   plus the wave-5 mini-boss composition, truncated by
   `truncateCampaignForDeployment` — never a hard-coded 5/10), ending on the
   wave-5 composition clear; the mini-boss encounter's own
   duration is **not** modelled; retries cost the measured replay; re-captures
   cost the measured mean + visit.

the emitted event. If simulating past the clear makes the regeneration
impractically slow, record the measured wall-clock cost and file a follow-up
item rather than changing `runArena` in this item.

- `createArenaDeploymentRunner` runs the arena in per-level mode at `request.level` and derives each deployment's `seconds` from the `level_cleared` event tick; no path reads `ticksSimulated` or `won` for a deployment's duration or outcome.

- A lost deployment's retry charge equals its own measured length × `retriesPerLoss`, and `DEFAULT_RETRY_MINUTES` is no longer charged by default (its doc comment or removal says so).
- The rush line's re-capture allowance charges the line's measured mean deployment + the documented 2-minute between-sortie visit; the 2-minute allowance itself is unchanged.

- No arena semantic change: `git show --stat` touches no other module's behaviour, or, if a shared seam proves unavoidable, the change is minimal, documented and covered by an arena test.
- The new model's tests pass and the full project test suite passes with the change.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` — the deployment runner (per-level mode, `level_cleared` duration/outcome), the retry and re-capture allowances, and the module documentation.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — read-only: the `level_cleared` event the runner reads (no second level-completion rule).
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` — the pinned semantics this item must turn green.

## Coordination (2026-11-13): the harness plays the shipped five-wave sortie

The deployment `createArenaDeploymentRunner` plays is the shipped **five-wave
sortie** (AH-0MWDCBVQ700579WS, on `dev`): the aggression-selected level's
first four regular waves plus the wave-5 mini-boss composition, truncated with
the same pure helper the game uses (`truncateCampaignForDeployment`,
`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`, `DEPLOYMENT_WAVE_COUNT = 5`) —
never a hard-coded 5 or 10. The harness keeps the arena's per-level mode (it
plays the level's authored waves) but must ensure the deployment's wave set is
the truncated one; if that needs a minimal shared arena seam (e.g. the wave
plan / level definition the per-level mode builds), it is allowed under the
"No arena semantic change" acceptance criterion when it is minimal, documented
and covered by an arena test. `level_cleared` then fires on the tick the
fifth wave's composition clears; the mini-boss encounter itself is not
simulated (the unmodelled fidelity gap).

## Impact

The ring-timing evidence now measures the sortie a player actually flies — one hex, one level, ending on the wave-5 mini-boss composition clear — so the Hangar War pacing budgets can be re-ruled from real measured numbers instead of a campaign slice that no longer ships.

artifact**.

## Context

The authored windows are ring 1 **40–60 min** and ring 2 **90–120 min**
(`RING_TIMING_TARGETS`), judged on the **grind** line with a 10 % tolerance of
each window's width (±2 min / ±3 min). One-level deployments should shrink ring
totals markedly (the retired model spent most of a deployment climbing campaign
levels past the hex's own), so a ring missing its window is the **expected**
outcome, not a defect in the new model — and the parent item's AC3 forbids
silently re-wording a missed budget: each missed ring becomes its own linked
rebalancing item.

Ring windows are **not** re-authored in this item: the harness records what the
shipped game measures, and a window change is a separate design decision.

## Desired change

1. Judge each ring's grind total from the regenerated artifact against its
   authored window and tolerance; state `in-window`, `within-tolerance` or
   `missed` per ring with the measured figure and the delta to the window.

   item carrying: the measured figure (mean + min–max), the window, the delta,
   the loss/retry/re-capture split that produces it, the before/after change
   attributable to the one-level model, and the options available (re-author the
   window, tune the authored ring data, revisit the retry/re-capture
   allowances) — leave the ruling to the producer. Link it with
   `related-to:AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A` and record the created ids on parent and
   this item.

   `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` reflect the regenerated numbers, and the
   ring-1/ring-2 verdicts are asserted explicitly so a future silent drift
   fails.

   data or the allowances here.

"Ends at its level's wave-10 clear" in the acceptance criterion above is
superseded: the shipped sortie (AH-0MWDCBVQ700579WS, on `dev`) is five waves

`truncateCampaignForDeployment` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`,
`DEPLOYMENT_WAVE_COUNT = 5`). The new-model test line therefore reads "a
per-level deployment ends at its level's wave-5 sortie clear"; everything

## Verdicts (2026-11-13, regenerated artifact)

Source: `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, regenerated from the shipped code
by AH-0MWCQ4GTE005YG02 (`npm run ring-timing -- --json --out
docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, two runs byte-identical, sha256
`d8fb5775…`). Judged on the **grind** line, seeds 1–3, against the authored

# Defense report should be rolled into the hex map screen

## Problem statement

The between-sortie defence report is a separate textual screen (`DefenceReportScene`) that the player must click through after every deployment, even though the hex map already knows every hex and its attack history. The report's information — which hexes were attacked, whether they held or fell, and the numbers behind it — belongs on the map itself, so the player sees the outcomes spatially, in the context of the ring, without an intermediate screen.

## Users

- **Hangar War player (primary):** after a deployment ends, wants to see at a glance where attacks occurred on the ring, and to inspect the numbers behind a specific attack by focusing the hex(es) involved — without a separate report screen.
  - *User story:* "When my deployment ends I land back on the hex map and see arrows showing where the frontier attacked. I move focus to the hex that fell and read on the left exactly what happened — attacking force, aggression, defender rating, margin — and what I need to do about it."
- **Attract-mode watcher:** the demo must never stall on (or have to click through) a removed screen; the map's arrows render from the same transient record and the demo continues exactly as it did from the report.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Flow: deployment ends on the hex map.** After a Hangar War deployment finishes, `PlayScene` starts `HexMapScene` directly (not `DefenceReportScene`), passing the tick record, the run result line (VICTORY/DEFEAT · score) and any won mini-boss reward; `DefenceReportScene` is removed from the shipped scene list and module surface (`src/core/gameConfig.ts`, `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.ts`), and a test drives the win path with no `DefenceReportScene` in the game config.
- **Attack arrows.** The hex map renders one arrow per attack in the most recent between-sortie tick record, from the attacker-origin hex to the attacked hex, positioned from the record's axial coordinates on the existing `axialToPixel` layout; the arrow data derives from a shared pure model (no per-scene rule), and a test asserts an arrow exists for every `record.attacks` entry and points at the correct target hex.
- **Left-hand attack-details panel.** When the focused hex is either endpoint of an attack arrow (the attacked hex OR its attacker-origin hex), a new panel on the LEFT of the map shows that attack's details (the numbers the resolved tick recorded — outcome, attacking force, aggression, defender rating, attack strength, margin, retake plan); the existing right-hand intel panel stays untouched; when the focused hex is not involved in any attack, the left panel hides. Tests pin the panel text for both endpoint kinds and its absence for an uninvolved hex.
- **Transient arrows, no persistence.** The arrows and attack panels reflect only the most recent between-sortie tick record carried from the deployment and are cleared when the map is re-entered without a record (e.g. from the menu/hangar later); no new payload field or store migration is introduced and no attack history is persisted.
- **Win-path reward still presents, over the paused map.** The mini-boss reward a winning deployment resolves is presented via the shipped `MiniBossWheelScene`/`MineralChoiceScene` overlay with the map paused, then the map resumes normal interaction; the existing win-path ordering test (reward → map interaction) is kept green by moving it onto the map.
- **Gym↔game parity maintained.** `GymHexWar` renders the same integrated map renderer (arrows + left attack panel) when given the same record, and its report view/`DEFENCE_REPORT` seam is updated or removed consistently; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` is updated to reflect the rolled-in report. The changed-scope test gate passes and the full suite stays green.
- **All related documentation updated.** Code comments, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D section, GDD §8.2 (defence report), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` and any README/wiki entries describing the between-sortie report screen reflect the rolled-in design, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Impact

Players no longer click through a separate textual report screen — after a deployment they land on the hex map where arrows show where the frontier attacked and the left panel explains the numbers behind any attack they focus.

## Constraints

- **View only, no re-derivation:** the arrows and attack panel copy every number from the tick record (via the shared `buildDefenceReport` model); no scene may recompute an attack, an outcome or a margin (gym↔game parity, AGENTS.md).
- **No store change:** nothing new is persisted; attacker-origin coordinates already travel in `FrontierTickRecord.attacks[]` (`attackerOrigin` + `hexId`), so arrows render from existing launch-data (transient, Q2 = a).
- **Parity surface:** the map renderer (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`) and its read model are shared with `GymHexWar`; any change must land there once (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).
- Pure models keep no Phaser imports in `src/core/hangarWar/`; UK English in UI strings.
- The shared `FocusManager` drives focus; the left panel keys off the focused row like the right panel does today.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene._finishRun` → `this.scene.start(DEFENCE_REPORT_SCENE_KEY, { payload, record, won, score, reward, demo, demoDwellMs })` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:5601` region).
- `DefenceReportScene` renders `buildDefenceReport(payload, record)` via `renderDefenceReport` and has one action (continue → map); win-path reward is presented over the paused report, then `_startMap()`.
- `HexMapScene` currently accepts `{ payload, storage, definitions, demo, demoDwellMs }` only — no record, no run line, no reward.
- `renderHexMap` already draws tiles via `axialToPixel(intel.q, intel.r)` and has a right-hand detail panel keyed to the focused hex (`PANEL_X = GAME_WIDTH - 260`); the left area (x ≈ 24) currently holds header lines and the HANGAR row.
- `FrontierTickRecord` carries `attacks[]`, each with `hexId`, `attackerOriginId`, `attackerOrigin { q, r }` and the full `DefenceResolution` numbers — everything an arrow and a details panel need.
- Gym: `GymHexWar` renders `renderHexMap` (map view) and `renderDefenceReport` (report view) with no handlers; parity pinned in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.
- Demo traversal: `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts` includes a `defenceReport` screen decision (`continueToMap`), driven by `decideReportAction`; `hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts` walks menu → hangar → map → deployment → report → map and pins win-path ordering (report → reward → map).

## Desired change

- `HexMapSceneData` gains `record?: FrontierTickRecord`, `won?: boolean | null`, `score?: number`, `reward?: MiniBossWinReward | null`; `PlayScene._finishRun` starts `HEX_MAP_SCENE_KEY` with these instead of the report scene.
- `buildHexMapModel` (or a sibling pure helper over the tick record) exposes the attack arrows (origin id/coords → target id) and the per-attack details keyed by hex id; `renderHexMap` draws arrows on the axial grid and adds a left-hand details panel that shows the attack block when the focused hex is an arrow endpoint, hiding otherwise.
- Win-path reward presentation moves from `DefenceReportScene` onto a paused `HexMapScene` (same overlay launch/resume contract); demo mode auto-resolves it as today.
- `DefenceReportScene` and its registration are deleted; `decideReportAction`/the `defenceReport` traversal screen are removed from `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts` and its tests (the map decision already never stalls).
- `GymHexWar` swaps its report view for the integrated map+arrows view (or drops the seam), and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` is updated.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_finishRun` deployment branch starts `HexMapScene` with record/run-line/reward instead of `DefenceReportScene`.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — new launch-data fields; reward-over-paused-map presentation; passes record into the shared renderer.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — draws attack arrows (origin → target via `axialToPixel`) and the left-hand attack-details panel.
- `src/core/hangarWar/defenceReport.ts` + `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — the shared pure model(s) exposing arrow + per-attack detail data from the record (kept Phaser-free).
- `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.ts` / `src/scenes/hangarWar/defenceReport.ts` — removed (or repurposed); `src/core/gameConfig.ts` scene list updated.
- `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts` (+ tests) — drop the `defenceReport` screen decision.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` + `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — gym renders the integrated map view.
- Tests: `src/scenes/hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts`, `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/hangarWar/defenceReport.test.ts`, `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.test.ts`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP** — Between-sortie defence report and attract-mode traversal (completed; the scene this item replaces).
- **AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2** — Hex map scene with known-ahead intel (completed; the map surface being extended).
- **AH-0MWBW1B1Z0059CC2** — In HexMap killing the mini-boss wins the hex (completed; parent of the win-path reward flow this item relocates).
- **AH-0MWCOW61X002LL10** — Tests: win-path ordering report then reward then map (completed; ordering test moves onto the map).
- **AH-0MWBBUAUQ0038GFL** — Defence report and intel render redistribution (completed; related report view-model work).
- **AH-0MWDBI33V003QQ3U** — Hangar Map UX (open; separate map-layout item — watch for left-panel layout overlap).
- **AH-0MW3VG6WJ004HRI9** — Text on hex map is unreadable (completed; the readability bar the new left panel must meet).
- Docs: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D, GDD §8.2 "The defence report", `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.

### Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MWDBI33V003QQ3U** – Hangar Map UX (open)
- **AH-0MW3VG6WJ004HRI9** – Text on hex map is unreadable (completed)
- **AH-0MUE86S5F002VVQD** – Leaderboard entry screen should show position in table (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `README.md` — matches the item's keywords (add/arrows/attack/…); check for claimed report-screen behaviour to update.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — contains the "defence report" (§8.2) and hex-map sections this item rewrites.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — keyword hits only, not directly affected.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — left/right panel overlap:** `AH-0MWDBI33V003QQ3U` (Hangar Map UX, open) may also move map UI around; the new left panel must not collide with the header/HANGAR rows on the left edge or the right intel panel when both land. Mitigation: place the attack panel in a dedicated left band and note the coordinate choice in the item; conflict is coordination-only (no shared file rule).
- **Risk — reward regression:** moving `_presentReward`/`_afterReward` from the report scene onto the map risks the "reward never shown" or "map unresponsive" failure modes; the shipped win-path test (`hangarWarFlow.integration.test.ts`) pins ordering and provides the red/green gate.
- **Risk — demo stall:** removing the report screen removes a traversal hop; the bot must continue straight from map → deploy → map, so `decideReportAction` removal must not leave a screen without a decision. Mitigation: the map decision (`decideMapAction`) is already total; traversal tests cover it.
- **Assumption — transient record:** arrows/panels reflect only the carried tick record and vanish on later map re-entry (Q2 = a); run result line and reward are carried once, like today.
- **Assumption — quiet tick:** a tick with no attacks draws no arrows and the left panel stays hidden (no new empty-state copy needed).
- **Scope-creep guard:** attack *history*, arrow styling/fancy VFX, and persistent per-attack storage are deliberately out of scope (Q2 = a); record them as separate work items rather than expanding this change.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Fate of `DefenceReportScene` and the win-path reward — (a) remove the scene, a deployment ends straight on the map carrying record + run line + reward, reward overlay over the paused map (recommended); (b) keep it as an optional deeper report behind a key; (c) repurpose into a transient report banner on the map." — Answer (producer): **a**. Source: producer reply 2026-11-13.
- Q2: "Arrow scope and persistence — (a) only the most recent between-sortie tick's attacks, transient, cleared when the map is re-entered later, no store migration (recommended); (b) persist attack history in the payload." — Answer (producer): **a**. Source: producer reply 2026-11-13.
- Q3: "Left panel semantics and 'hexes involved' — (a) new LEFT attack-details panel when the focused hex is either arrow endpoint, right-hand intel panel stays, hides when not involved (recommended); (b) replace the right-hand panel; (c) only the attacked target shows details." — Answer (producer): **a**. Source: producer reply 2026-11-13.

# Rebalance ring 1's grind budget: measured 16.4 min against the authored 40–60 min window

Discovered-from: AH-0MWCQ4HTC004U73V (Budget verdicts and linked rebalancing
items), part of the re-measurement chain under AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A (Re-measure
ring timing for one-level hex deployments). **Producer ruling required** — this
item records the evidence and the options; it does not decide which way the
budget should move.

## Why this item exists

`RING_TIMING_TARGETS` authors ring 1's grind window as **40–60 minutes** with a
±10 % tolerance of the window's width (**±2 minutes**), judged on the **grind**
line. The regenerated artifact (`docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, produced
by `AH-0MWCQ4GTE005YG02` from the shipped code) measures the shipped one-level
five-wave sortie at **16.4 minutes**, so the authored window no longer holds.
The parent's acceptance criteria forbid silently re-wording a missed budget,
so the miss is recorded here and the ruling is left to the producer.

## Measurement (source: `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json`, ring 1, `grind`, seeds 1–3)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verdict | **missed** (`withinWindow: false`, `withinTolerance: false`) |
| Measured total mean | **16.4256 min** (seeds: 15.7239 / 16.6383 / 16.9144) |
| Measured total min–max | **15.7239 – 16.9144 min** |
| Authored window | **40 – 60 min** |
| Tolerance | ±10 % of window width = **±2 min** (tolerance floor 38 min) |
| Delta to window floor | **−23.5744 min** below 40 min; **−21.5744 min** below the 38 min tolerance floor |
| Deployment minutes (measured, mean) | 2.2128 (1.8619 / 2.3192 / 2.4572) |
| Between-sortie minutes (modelled) | 12.0 (2 min × 6 hexes) |
| Retry minutes (measured replay) | 2.2128 (= the replayed deployment's measured length) |
| Re-capture minutes (modelled) | 0.0 (the grind line secures the ring) |
| Split check | 2.2128 + 12.0 + 2.2128 + 0.0 = 16.4256 = the total mean |
| Captured / lost sorties | 0.0 / **6.0** per run — every sortie is a first-attempt loss to enemy fire and is retried |
| Ring secured | 3 / 3 runs (the grind plays every hex, so the ring still ends secured) |
| Salvage | 0.0 banked, 15.0 forfeited (mean: 25 / 4 / 16) |

## Before/after attributable to the one-level model

| Ring 1 grind | Before (campaign slice) | After (one-level sortie) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total mean (min–max) | 54.3 (51.0–56.6) | **16.4 (15.7–16.9)** | −37.9 min |
| Verdict | in-window (40–60) | **missed (40–60)** | window no longer holds |
| Deployment minutes | 19.0 | 2.2 | −16.8 (the slice no longer climbs campaign levels past the hex's own) |
| Retry minutes | 23.3 | 2.2 | −21.1 (retry now charges the replayed deployment's measured length, not a flat 5 min) |
| Between-sortie minutes | 12.0 | 12.0 | unchanged (2 min × 6 hexes) |
| Re-capture minutes | 0.0 | 0.0 | unchanged on the grind line |
| Captured / lost | 1.3 / 4.7 | 0.0 / 6.0 | no sortie clears under the per-level arena's fire-on fidelity |
| Salvage banked / forfeited | 24.0 / 54.0 | 0.0 / 15.0 | no capture ⇒ no banking |

The dominant driver is the deployment model itself: a deployment's measured
arena time fell from ≈3.2 min to ≈0.4 min, and the retry term follows it
mechanically (retry = the replayed deployment's measured length). The
between-sortie allowance (2 min) and the re-capture allowance are unchanged and
do not drive the delta.

## Options (for the producer; not a recommendation)

1. **Re-author the ring-1 window** (e.g. from 40–60 min to a window the shipped

## Problem

When `implement.py drive` spawns a child session that dies before writing anything (e.g. a transient provider error — `Provider finish_reason: error`), the child is left `in-progress` with an empty worktree (0 dirty files, 0 commits ahead of dev). The next `drive`/`parent` run then calls `_child_main_checkout_violation()` for that child, which finds `_git_path_has_changes(wt)` false (correctly — no work) and therefore attributes **pre-existing dirt in the main checkout and in other items' sibling worktrees** to the failed child. The run fails closed with a long 'produced changes in the sibling worktree …' message naming paths the child never touched.

## Impact during AH-0MWDC3L9I008INDP

Recovering child AH-0MWEXI5460080WEI required a manual `implement.py abort` before the drive would proceed; the guard's message blamed `src/test/playSceneBootGuard.test.ts` (main checkout) and files in `wl-AH-0MTVYBL2L0085G6G`, `wl-AH-0MVAUU594007S92Q`, `wl-AH-0MWCOWTOR00994NA` and `/tmp/hw-base-check` — all other sessions' work.

## Acceptance criteria

- A driven child left `in-progress` by a **spawn failure** (no changes in its worktree, no commits ahead) is treated as startable-again/reset, not as a placement violation, so the next `drive` re-spawns it without manual `abort`.
- The placement guard distinguishes 'this child wrote elsewhere' from 'this child wrote nothing and other surfaces happen to be dirty' — the latter must not fail the chain.
- Regression test: a spawn-failed child plus a dirty main checkout and a dirty sibling worktree does not produce a `_child_main_checkout_violation`; a child that genuinely wrote only into a sibling worktree still does.
- No weakening of the genuine cross-worktree-write detection (SA-0MW5FIJNQ002Z24I).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVFBCVIS007BN81** – implement.py: behind-only child worktree mis-detected as 'has changes' and auto-finished (completed)

## Scope and repository location

**The defect is not in this repository.** The placement guard lives in
`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, which resides in the **SorraAgents**
repository (the global skill at `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement` is a symlink
into it). AI_Hell contains no `implement.py`, so this item is the **discovery

2026-11-14, stage `plan_complete`, children SA-0MWGZ8E7C001X2HA Test and

**Key Files:**

## Impact

The intermittent SceneNavigation AC4 flake is gone: a boss victory reliably returns the player to the menu from GameOverScene under full parallel suite load, and the deterministic stepping helpers resolve the hold-full pause so the win transition can no longer stall.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `src/scenes/SceneNavigation.test.ts > Scene navigation — Menu → Play → GameOver → Menu (AH-0MU731IIZ001SQLA) > AC4 — a boss victory also returns to the menu from GameOverScene` passes when run against the latest `dev`.

2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

## Plan (plan skill session, 2026-11-13)

### History — recurrence

This is the **fourth** occurrence of the same test in the worklog, and the third
distinct stall mechanism:

| Item | Mechanism | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AH-0MUR0FNCW001SCNE | RNG-sequenced waves / real-time waits | deterministic static campaign |
| AH-0MUINWNPI000G6MU | file timeout (5 s) breached under parallel load | `vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 120000 })` |
| AH-0MV6OEPQG009YKMS | hold-full choice paused the scene mid-walk | `reachBoss` + `resolveMineralChoiceIfOpen` |
| **this item** | hold-full choice pauses the scene **inside the boss-kill / victory-hold window** | planned below |

Because three successive harness patches have not stopped the recurrence, this
plan targets the *mechanism* (an unguarded pause state in the deterministic
stepping path) rather than widening a timeout again.

### Root cause analysis (plan-time, from repository evidence)

Observed signature: `stepUntil(GameOverScene active): condition not met after
600 steps; active=[PlayScene]` — the **win transition** never fired, unlike the
previous walk stalls.

Mechanism, with code references:

1. `_damageBoss()` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` ~3604) sets `runFinished = true`,
   triggers the victory celebration and calls `_finishRunWithPurpose(true)`,
   which schedules the scene change with
   `this.time.delayedCall(VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS, …)` (~4600).
   `VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS = ENDOFRUN_VICTORY_FIREWORKS_DURATION_MS = 5000`
   (`src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts:137`) — i.e. **≈300 fixed steps at 16.67 ms**,
   half of `stepUntil`'s 600-step budget.
2. The AC4 kill loop (`src/scenes/SceneNavigation.test.ts` ~424) spawns one
   bullet and ticks `boss.getTotalHp()` times **without** the
   `resolveMineralChoiceIfOpen` guard that `reachBoss` and `killMiniBoss` use.
   Phase depletions summon minions (`_spawnMinions`); killed minions and
   asteroids drop minerals.
3. When the hold fills, `openMineralChoice()` (~6155) calls `setPaused(true)`
   and `tick()` returns immediately while paused (~1843). Every remaining
   kill-loop tick *and* every subsequent `game.step` — including the 300-step
   victory `delayedCall` — becomes a no-op.
4. Result: the boss may not even die (`runFinished` never set) and the win can
   never transition, so `stepUntil` exhausts its budget with
   `active=[PlayScene]` — the exact reported signature. The
   `MineralChoiceScene` is not registered in this suite's boot
   (`[MenuScene, PlayScene, GameOverScene, GymIndex]`), so no scene-level pause
   short-circuits the loop; the stall is purely the `paused` flag.
5. `resolveMineralChoiceIfOpen` is **duplicated** in
   `src/scenes/SceneNavigation.test.ts` and
   `src/scenes/PlayScene.campaignLevelClear.test.ts`, and the shared harness
   helper `stepGameUntil` (`src/test/gameHarness.ts:329`) has the same blind
   spot — so the guard cannot be applied uniformly and every new walker can
   reintroduce the flake.

**Secondary (product) defect.** A mineral collected after the boss dies can open
a pausing reward overlay on an **already-finished** run; the player then faces a
run-scoped upgrade choice whose effect is void, and the screen change waits on
it. This is the same "run-scoped reward applied to a completed run" principle
the producer already ruled against for the hangar win path
(AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2, Q1 = (c)). The hold-full choice lives only in
`PlayScene`/`CombatScene` (gyms run `GymFormationScene` ← `CombatCoreScene` and
have no `runFinished`), so the guard is a game-only no-op in the gyms — to be
confirmed and recorded against `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.

### Features (test-first, dependency-ordered)

1. **Test + diagnostics for the victory-path stall** (`task`, high) — reproduce
   the pause deterministically and make future stalls self-diagnosing.
2. **Harden deterministic stepping** (`task`, high) — one shared hold-full
   resolver, applied to the kill loop and to `stepUntil`/`stepGameUntil`.
   Depends on 1.
3. **Suppress the hold-full choice after the run finishes** (`bug`, medium) —
   stop offering a void reward on a won run. Depends on 1.
4. **Docs + full-suite verification** (`docs`, medium) — README testing
   conventions, flake lineage, and the shipped green suite. Depends on 2 and 3.

### Phasing decision

This is **not** a phased epic: the four children are sequential increments of a
single defect (reproduce → harness hardening → product guard → document and
verify), each carrying its own tests and doc touch. No horizontal layer is
deferred, so no between-phase review gate is required; items 2 and 3 each update
the next item's description if the reproduction in item 1 changes the diagnosis.

### Documented assumptions

1. The stall is the hold-full pause inside the boss-kill / victory-hold window
   (evidence above); a widening of `stepUntil`'s budget is **not** the fix,
   because a paused scene ignores time entirely.
2. The fix stays inside test harness helpers plus one narrow `PlayScene` guard —
   no boss, wave, reward or balance changes.
3. The stray untracked `src/test/playSceneBootGuard.test.ts` in the main
   checkout is already tracked elsewhere (AH-0MWFI3BLE000JMRU,
   AH-0MWFHXYGW003L1VM) and must not be edited or deleted by this work.

### Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No producer interview was required.** Every planning input was derived from
  repository evidence (source, worklog history, prior items) and recorded in the
  RCA above; no question was put to the producer in this session.

- **OPEN QUESTION (producer; non-blocking, resolved by feature 1):** is the
  hold-full-during-victory pause reachable by a human player (a live product
  defect: a void reward overlay on a won run, whose selection gates the
  GameOverScene transition), or only reachable through deterministic test
  stepping? Feature 1's reproduction records the answer; if it is
  human-reachable, feature 3 is a product fix (with gym-parity note) rather than
  a test-only guard. Planning proceeds on the conservative assumption that it is
  reachable and worth guarding.

# Conflict markers committed to docs/GYM_PARITY.md on dev

## Problem statement

dev's `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` carried committed Git merge-conflict markers
(`<<<<<<< HEAD` / `=======` / `>>>>>>> ef87a124`) from an earlier merge, so the
published parity matrix contained two nested three-way conflict blocks that
split the `GymHangar` / `GymHexWar` table rows and the defending-bot-skills vs
special-mission prose. The markers have since been removed while keeping both
sides' content (commit `fd68cd53`, child `AH-0MWEWYZLQ0078G0D`), but nothing
detects a recurrence: the existing docs guard
(`src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts`) validates scene coverage, verdicts
and evidence — not file integrity — so a future bad merge could land markers on
dev again unnoticed.

## Users

- **The maintainer / parity-sweep owner** reading the matrix to decide whether a
  gym has diverged.
  - *As a maintainer, I want one clean, unambiguous matrix, so I can trust a
    row's verdict without decoding conflict noise.*
- **The agent making a gym↔game parity change**, sent to this file by `AGENTS.md`
  § Game Architecture Conventions.
  - *As an agent, I want a corrupted merge to fail the test suite, so I never
    read, act on or extend a half-merged matrix.*
- **The producer reviewing dev.**
  - *As a producer, I want committed conflict markers caught by a test rather
    than by a human reader.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` contains no Git merge-conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`,
  `=======`, `>>>>>>>`) and both sides of the original merge are preserved —
  the `GymHangar` special-missions note, and the `GymHexWar` defending-bot
  skills, special missions and ring-end hangar assault. Verification:
  `grep -nE '^(<{7}|={7}|>{7})' docs/GYM_PARITY.md` returns nothing, and the
  existing row/prose assertions in `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts`
  still pass.
- `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` gains a guard assertion that reads
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` and fails when any conflict marker is present, reporting
  the offending line numbers so the bad merge is actionable.
- The new guard is proven non-vacuous by a red-before test that injects markers
  into an in-memory copy (or a temporary fixture) of the real document and
  asserts the detector reports them — without mutating the repository, matching
  the existing red-before pattern in that file.
- The `Automated guard` panel in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` states that the guard
  also fails if the file contains merge-conflict markers, so the documented
  guard matches the test that enforces it.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. Full project
  test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A maintainer or agent reading `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` sees one clean parity matrix
instead of three-way conflict noise, and a future bad merge now fails the test
suite instead of quietly landing conflict markers on dev.

## Constraints

- **Preserve both sides.** The original merge's content on both sides is
  intentional: do not "resolve" the history by dropping the defending-bot-skills
  or special-mission text. `fd68cd53` already removed the markers correctly;
  this item must not undo that.
- **Extend the existing docs guard.** The assertion belongs in
  `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts`, alongside the other matrix guards —
  no new test framework, script or pre-commit hook.
- **No repository mutation in the red-before case.** Prove the guard fails
  against an in-memory/fixture copy, never by writing markers into the real doc.
- **Avoid false positives.** A bare `=======` line is also a legal Markdown
  setext heading underline; anchor the detector on the conflict-marker lines and,
  if `=======` is matched, require it inside a `<<<<<<<` … `>>>>>>>` block (the
  document currently has neither setext headings nor marker lines).
- **Docs + test only.** No gameplay or source behaviour changes; the gym↔game
  parity convention itself is untouched.
- Run tests only through the test skill (`/skill:test`); do not invoke `pytest`,
  `vitest` or equivalent directly.

## Existing state

- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` currently has **zero** conflict markers (verified with
  `grep -nE '^(<{7}|={7}|>{7})'`), after `fd68cd53` removed them and kept both
  sides' content. The file also has no setext headings, so all three marker

## Goal

**As an** arcade player, **I want** no reward choice to open after I have already won the run, **so that** the victory celebration leads straight to the score screen instead of a void upgrade pick whose effect can never be used.

## Context

Parent RCA step 3: a mineral collected after the boss dies (lingering drops, phase minions, asteroids) can fill the hold and call `openMineralChoice()` → `setPaused(true)` on an **already-finished** run (`runFinished === true`). The player is offered run-scoped upgrades with no run left to use them in, and the `GameOverScene` transition waits on that choice. This follows the producer's already-recorded principle for the hangar win path (`AH-0MWEVNBMM000QFO2`, Q1 = (c): run-scoped rewards must not be presented on a completed run).

The hold-full choice lives in `PlayScene` only — gyms run `GymFormationScene` ← `CombatCoreScene` and have no `runFinished` state — so this must be confirmed as a documented game-only guard (or extended to the shared core if gyms ever gain a run-finished concept), per the gym↔game parity rule in `AGENTS.md`.

## Deliverables

- `_requestHoldFullChoice()` (and `_flushPendingHoldFullChoice()`) no-op once the run has finished: minerals are still credited, no overlay is opened, and any deferred (pending) hold-full request is dropped rather than opened later.
- A test that asserts the guard: with `runFinished` true (a won run), collecting a hold-filling mineral opens no choice and the win transition still completes.
- A comment recording the gym-parity check (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` vs `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` / `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`) and, if a divergence is introduced, an entry in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` with its reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With the run finished (`runFinished === true`) and the hold full, `isMineralChoiceOpen()` stays false and no overlay is launched; the collected mineral is still credited to `gameState.minerals`.
2. A deferred hold-full request queued before the boss died is cleared on a won run and never opens after `_finishRun`, so the `VICTORY_TRANSITION_HOLD_MS` → `GameOverScene` transition is never gated by a choice.
3. A test covers both the direct request and the deferred (pending) request; both fail before the guard and pass after it.
4. The loss path and the mid-run hold-full behaviour are unchanged: the existing hold-full choice suites pass unmodified.
5. The gym-parity check is recorded in a comment on this item, and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` carries an entry only if a divergence actually exists.
6. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean and the changed-scope suite green through `/skill:test`.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_requestHoldFullChoice`, `_flushPendingHoldFullChoice`, `runFinished`, `_collectMineral`, `_damageBoss`, `isRunFinished()`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.campaignLevelClear.test.ts` / the hold-full choice suites — existing expectations to preserve.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — parity comparison.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — only if a divergence is documented.


## Impact

After a run is won, a mineral that fills the hold after the boss dies no longer pops a void upgrade choice — the victory celebration flows straight to the score screen.

# Hangar War: leave the defending bot with the run's permanent upgrades

## Problem statement

When a hex deployment is won, the bot left behind carries only the **catalogue** hull rating (`baseDefence + 3 × armour + 2 × firepower + 2 × systems` of the hull as authored in the hangar catalogue), so everything the ship actually earned during that sortie — permanent weapon levels, permanent power-up levels and owned consumable charges — is discarded at the moment of victory. A player who clears a hex with a heavily upgraded ship leaves a bot no stronger than a bare hull, which makes the capture's "leave a bot" step feel disconnected from the run that earned it.

## Users and user stories

- **Player (primary).** "When I beat a hex's mini-boss, I want the bot I leave behind to keep the permanent upgrades my ship had at that moment, so the run I just flew is what defends the hex."
- **Player, reading the map.** "When I look at a held hex, I want to see what the defending bot is made of — its upgrade contribution and total rating — so I can judge whether the next frontier attack will hold."
- **Designer/tuner (secondary).** "I want the upgrade → rating conversion in one documented table, so retuning defence strength never needs a code change or a save migration."

## Existing state

- `leaveDefender` (`src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts`) builds the `HexDefender` with `defenceRating = deriveDefenderRating(hullId)`, plus optional boss-typed `skills` from the hull and equipped modifiers.
- `deriveDefenderRating` / `defenderRatingFromUpgrades` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) are the single rating formula, fed only from the hangar catalogue.
- `HexCaptureInput` carries `hexId`, `defenderHullId`, `salvage`, `definitions`, `banked`, `tuning` — **no run-upgrade snapshot**.
- At the mini-boss victory the run does hold the data: `Player.getWeaponLevels()`, `Player.getPowerUpLevels()`, and `PowerUpLevelStore.snapshotConsumablePools()` (read by `_saveCheckpoint` for the arcade path, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`).
- The defender is never flown; every defence is arithmetic over stored numbers (`resolveDefence`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`).
- Design of record explicitly says the rating comes from the hull's hangar upgrades only: GDD *capture cycle* step 3 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (intake assumption A4). This item changes that rule.
- The frontier aggression budget is sized from `resolvePlayerStrength(hangar)` — hangar progression only — and the *between-sortie tick* compares each held hex's stored rating against `baseAttackingForce (2) + origin aggression × 1`, scaled by `100 + 15 × aggression` % ± 10 %.

## Desired change

1. **Snapshot the run at victory.** `resolveHexCapture` accepts the run's permanent-upgrade snapshot and `leaveDefender` persists it on the `HexDefender` as an **additive optional field** (same back-compat pattern as `skills`): permanent weapon levels, permanent power-up levels, and the owned consumable charge state.
2. **Convert it with the hull's own vocabulary.** The snapshot contributes to the rating through one documented mapping table, so the rating stays a single number the resolver compares:

   | Source | Stat bucket | Weight |
   |---|---|---|
   | every permanent weapon level (any weapon) | firepower | 1 point per level |
   | permanent level of a **defensive** power-up kind (Shield, Force Field, Thorn Field, Bomb, Smart Bomb, Phase Shift) | armour | 1 point per level |
   | permanent level of every other power-up kind (Teleport, Speed Boost, Frenzy, Chrono, Magnet, Mineral Scoop, Mystery UFO, Salvage, Strike, Mining Laser) | systems | 1 point per level |
   | each held **defensive** consumable charge (Shield, Force Field, Thorn Field) | armour | 1 point per charge |
   | each held **other** consumable charge (Mystery UFO) | systems | 1 point per charge |

   Then `defenceRating = hullRating + 3 × armour + 2 × firepower + 2 × systems`, reusing the shipped `defenderRatingFromUpgrades` weights so there is still exactly one rating formula.
3. **Show the numbers.** The map's held-hex detail panel and the between-sortie defence report list the bot's stored upgrade breakdown next to the existing hull/skills lines, so a hold or fall that depended on upgrades is legible.
4. **One code path for the game and the gyms.** `GymHexWar`'s "leave bot" control surface takes the same snapshot and renders through the shared helpers (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity); no second derivation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `leaveDefender` / `resolveHexCapture` persist the run's permanent-upgrade snapshot on the `HexDefender` and derive `defenceRating = hullRating + 3 × armour + 2 × firepower + 2 × systems`, where the stat buckets come from one exported, documented mapping table that classifies **every** `WeaponId` and `PowerUpId` (a test fails if a catalogue id is unclassified).
- A defender captured with no permanent upgrades produces exactly today's payload and today's `defenceRating` (the new field is omitted when empty), so existing saves, fixtures and replays are unchanged; a save written before this change still loads and resolves as before.
- The `HexMapScene` held-hex detail panel and the between-sortie defence report show the left bot's stored armour/firepower/systems, the upgrade rating contribution and the total rating, alongside the existing hull and skill lines; `GymHexWar` leaves an upgraded bot through the same shared leave/derive/render code and displays the same numbers, with no divergent copy of the conversion (parity asserted by test).
- Tests cover: the mapping table (every id classified, unknown ids ignored), derivation totals, corrupt input (negative / fractional / non-finite snapshot collapses without throwing), the no-upgrades equality case, capture-cycle persistence and omission, `HexDefender` store round-trip/migration, and a `PlayScene`/`HexMapScene` assertion that a mini-boss victory persists the flown run's upgrades on the defender.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically GDD *capture cycle* step 3, the GDD defender-rating formula section, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (assumption A4) and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` for the gym control surface.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who wins a hex can now leave behind a bot that keeps the permanent upgrades the ship had when the mini-boss fell, and can read on the map exactly what that bot is worth.

## Out of scope

- Changing `resolvePlayerStrength` or the `DEFAULT_FRONTIER_TUNING` constants (producer decision Q3 = A).
- Carrying the run's **temporary** (timed) weapons or field-pickup state into the defender.
- Carrying held minerals, score or remaining lives onto the defender (not upgrades — see Assumptions).
- Any new defender behaviour in combat: the bot is still never flown; the defence stays arithmetic over stored numbers.

## Verification (manual)

1. Deploy at an unheld hex from the map, deliberately collect several permanent upgrades during the sortie, then beat the wave-5 mini-boss.
2. Re-open the map, focus the newly held hex and confirm the detail panel lists the upgrade breakdown and a total rating greater than the bare-hull rating.
3. Run one between-sortie tick and confirm the defence report shows the same stored rating on the attack row.
4. Repeat in `GymHexWar`'s leave-bot control surface and confirm identical numbers.

## Constraints

- **Pure and injectable:** the conversion and the derivation stay in the pure core (`captureCycle` / `hangarEconomy`), no Phaser, no storage access; the scene only supplies the snapshot and persists the returned payload.
- **No schema version bump:** the new field is additive/optional and read by field presence, matching `skills`, `frontierTick` and the contract fields.
- **One rating formula:** the resolver keeps comparing one stored `defenceRating`; nothing new enters `resolveDefence`.
- **Producer decisions recorded in this intake:** Q1 = B (weapon levels + power-up levels + owned consumable charges), Q2 = B (hull weights: armour 3 / firepower 2 / systems 2 via a per-kind mapping table), Q3 = A (the frontier aggression budget is **unchanged** — defence simply gets easier).
- **Balance consequence accepted (Q3 = A):** with shipped tuning the attack strength tops out near 26–28, so an upgrade contribution in the tens makes a held hex mathematically unretakeable, and the between-sortie tick's retake pressure effectively disappears for well-defended hexes.
- CHANGELOG.md is out of scope (managed by the release pipeline).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — new optional `HexDefender` upgrade-snapshot field (additive, omitted when empty).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — the mapping table, the snapshot → stat-bucket reducer and the extended rating derivation.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — `HexCaptureInput` gains the snapshot; `leaveDefender` / `resolveHexCapture` thread it through and record it on the defender.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — supplies `getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` / `snapshotConsumablePools()` at the mini-boss victory capture, in the same place the checkpoint snapshot is taken.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — defensive parsing of the new optional field (round-trip, migration by field presence).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` and `src/core/hangarWar/defenceReport.ts` — intel lines and report numbers for the stored breakdown.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — renders the new intel lines (shared with the gym).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — the "leave bot" control surface passes the snapshot and shows the same numbers.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — the rule change and its documented consequence.

## Related work

- Hangar War: capture cycle — hex deployment, boss-granted discovery and defending bot (AH-0MVUXCAW0001VUM6) — the module this changes.
- Pure defence resolver and frontier aggression clock (AH-0MVUXCA0J0011W88) — records the "rating from the hull's hangar upgrades, never a live battle" rule this item revises.
- Post-MVP Hangar War: upgraded defending bots with special skills (AH-0MVWZYJ740037EZ1) — the precedent for adding stored defender data additively.
- Versioned ai_hell_hangar_war store with migration (AH-0MVUXC0M5007LCGV) — the back-compat pattern the new optional field follows.
- Hangar economy and unlock tree (AH-0MVUXC1GQ00366Z6) — owns `deriveDefenderRating`, the weights and `resolvePlayerStrength`.
- Between-sortie defence report and attract-mode traversal (AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP) — the report surface that must show the new numbers.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Balance risk (highest):** with Q3 = A the frontier cannot outgrow upgraded defenders. A late run's upgrade contribution can exceed the maximum possible attack strength, so hexes become permanently safe and the war's retake tension goes quiet. *Mitigation:* the conversion lives in one exported table with one weight per bucket, so a follow-up tuning item can cap or rescale without touching saves; the risk should be measured from real runs before any such item is filed.
- **Save-compatibility risk:** an additive optional field on `HexDefender` must be omitted when empty and parsed defensively, or existing saves/fixtures drift. *Mitigation:* the `skills` pattern exactly; a store round-trip test and a "pre-change save loads unchanged" test.
- **Inflation risk:** consumable charge state changes between the mini-boss moment and the capture write if read at different points. *Mitigation:* read the whole snapshot once, in the same expression that feeds `resolveHexCapture`.
- **Design-document drift risk:** GDD step 3 and Candidate D A4 state the hangar-only rule; leaving them stale contradicts shipped behaviour. *Mitigation:* the docs AC names both files.
- **Scope-creep risk:** candidates deliberately excluded — changing `resolvePlayerStrength` (Q3 = A), retuning the frontier tuning constants, and carrying the run's *temporary* (timed) weapons into the defender. Each is a separate decision and must become its own work item rather than growing this one.
- **Assumption:** "permanent upgrades present at the end of the mini-boss battle" means the permanent levels and owned consumable charges the ship held at victory; held minerals, score and remaining lives are **not** upgrades and are not carried.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — What counts as "all permanent upgrades"?** Options: (A) permanent weapon levels + power-up levels; (B) A plus owned consumable charge pools; (C) everything permanent including extra lives and held minerals. — **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** **B** — permanent weapon levels, permanent power-up levels and owned consumable charges. *Research:* `playerPowerScore` (`src/core/difficultyScaling.ts`) already totals permanent weapon + power-up levels; `PowerUpLevelStore.snapshotConsumablePools()` exposes the owned consumable charge state.
- **Q2 — How do those upgrades become defence strength?** Options: (A) one documented weight per upgrade level; (B) reuse the hull weights (armour 3 / firepower 2 / systems 2) via a per-kind mapping; (C) apply them as boss-typed skills instead. — **Answer (operator):** **B** — keep one rating formula by mapping each weapon/power-up kind to armour, firepower or systems and applying the shipped weights. *Research:* `defenderRatingFromUpgrades(baseDefence, upgrades)` in `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` is the only rating formula; hull upgrades use armour/firepower/systems, so a per-kind mapping reuses it unchanged.
- **Q3 — Should the frontier aggression budget grow to match upgraded defenders?** Options: (A) leave the budget alone (defence gets easier); (B) count held defenders into `resolvePlayerStrength`; (C) cap the per-bot upgrade contribution. — **Answer (operator):** **A** — the budget is unchanged; the easier defence is accepted. *Research:* `resolvePlayerStrength` is fed from the hangar only, and tick attack strength derives from `baseAttackingForce: 2`, `forcePerOriginAggression: 1`, `aggressionPercentPerPoint: 15`, `jitterPercent: 10` (`DEFAULT_FRONTIER_TUNING`), i.e. a maximum near 26–28.
- **Q: How is "permanent" distinguished from a temporary field pickup at the victory moment?** — Answer (agent, from repo evidence): `Player.getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` report **permanent levels only** (`getTempWeaponIds()` / `getTempPowerUpIds()` are separate), so reading the permanent accessors at victory is exactly the requested set. No producer input needed.

Child of AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ (Hangar War: leave the defending bot with the run's permanent upgrades). Test-first verification item: the guard tests that pin the whole contract before any implementation lands, so the conversion table cannot drift and no catalogue id can escape classification.

As a developer, I want a test suite that fails until every `WeaponId` and `PowerUpId` has a documented stat bucket and the rating derivation is proven, so the upgrade → rating conversion can never silently regress or lose a newly added catalogue id.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Catalogue coverage is mechanically enforced.** A test iterates every key of the shipped `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` (`src/utils/weapons.ts`) and every member of `PowerUpId` (`src/powerups/types.ts`) and asserts each resolves a defined stat bucket; a deliberately unclassified id makes the assertion fail (proven by a negative test case over an injected partial table).

Child of AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ. `HexCaptureInput` accepts the victory-moment snapshot, `leaveDefender` records it on the defender, and the stored `defenceRating` becomes hull rating **plus** the snapshot's weighted contribution — still one number for the resolver.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, when I beat a hex's mini-boss, I want the bot I leave behind to keep the permanent upgrades my ship had at that moment, so the run I just flew is what defends the hex.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `HexCaptureInput` gains an optional permanent-upgrade snapshot; `leaveDefender` / `resolveHexCapture` persist it on the `HexDefender` and derive `defenceRating = hullRating + 3 × armour + 2 × firepower + 2 × systems` through the C2 helpers.
